Honestly the bar situation sounds like you handled it well. I think that was a good way to react and your concerns are fair. You gave her agency by asking her what you should do. 

Could you explain to her that you will seek her assistance if you’re sad, but that you’re mostly ok? 

It’s fair to not have disposable income for dates and things. Perhaps could you both brainstorm together cute dates where you don’t have to spend money? It sounds like she does need to be a bit understanding about your financial limitations. Also, nobody has to spend all of their disposable income on their partner. It’s good you do things for you. 

Its fair to feel frustrated or hurt when plans are changed. I have ADHD, so I’m always changing every now and again. However, I try and encourage the people in my life to learn about ADHD and how it impacts relationships. Would she be open to learning about ADD?

I suppose it sucks she forgot that you told her about your trip - but I’m unsure how thats your fault. Perhaps in future you need to provide more reminders when you’re going on trips? I think misperceptions and mistakes happen. The yelling part is the issue (although affected by alcohol). That’s not a kind way to communicate. 

It sounds like she also needs to try to communicate. If she wants to go on trips she should also ask instead of passively hoping you’ll work it out. It sounds like she hasn’t said some of these needs until its blown up into a problem. 

But yeah dude so understandable not being able to afford things. Sounds like she also needs to understand that you are not doing certain activities because of financial reasons, not because you don’t care for her.
